u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Yesterday my brother ________ his bike to the park.
u0.explanation: 'Yesterday' tells us it happened in the past, so we use the simple past tense. The past tense of ride is rode.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Last night we ________ at home because it was raining.
u0.explanation: We use 'were' with we, you and they in the past. 'Was' goes with I, he, she and it.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Amy ________ her homework last night. She forgot!
u0.explanation: Negatives in the past: didn't + the base verb. So we say 'didn't do', never 'didn't did'.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

________ you visit your grandma last Sunday?
u0.explanation: Questions in the past use Did + subject + base verb: Did you visit…?

The baby ________ (cry) all night, so Mum was very tired.

mark_scheme: cried (spelling must be correct: consonant + y → change y to i and add -ed)

u0.explanation: 'Cry' ends in consonant + y, so change y to i and add -ed: cried.

u0.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the given verb.

Two days ago, Ken ________ (stop) at the shop and bought some bread.
u0.explanation: 'Stop' has one vowel and one consonant at the end, so we double the p: stopped.

u0.stem:
Read Ka Yan's diary and fill in the blanks with the correct form of the given verbs.

mark_scheme: Answer: didn't see / did not see

u0.explanation: A diary tells about the past, so every verb is in the simple past tense. Go, swim, build and have are irregular: went, swam, built, had. The negative is didn't + base verb: didn't see.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

My sister ________ the piano every Sunday.
u1.explanation: 'Every Sunday' is a habit, so we use the simple present. With he/she/it we add -s: plays.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Look! The children ________ in the rain.
u1.explanation: 'Look!' tells us it is happening now, so we use the present continuous. 'The children' is plural: are dancing.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Tom ________ eat vegetables. He doesn't like them.
u1.explanation: With he/she/it, the negative is doesn't + base verb: Tom doesn't eat vegetables.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which sentence is correct?
u1.explanation: Adverbs of frequency go after am/is/are: She is always happy.

u1.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the given verb.

My dad ________ (watch) the news every evening.
u1.explanation: 'Every evening' is a habit. Verbs ending in ch add -es with he/she/it: watches.

u1.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the given verb.

Be quiet! The baby ________ (sleep) now.
u1.explanation: 'Now' tells us it is happening at the moment: is + verb-ing = is sleeping.

u1.stem:
Rewrite the sentence using the word in brackets.

I go swimming on Saturdays. (usually)

mark_scheme: I usually go swimming on Saturdays. (usually must come before 'go')

u1.explanation: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb: I usually go swimming on Saturdays.

u1.stem:
Read Mei's message and fill in the blanks with the correct form of the given verbs.

Hi Grandma! It's Sunday morning. Right now, I (1) ________ (sit) in the living room. Dad (2) ________ (cook) breakfast in the kitchen. On weekdays, he (3) ________ (go) to work at seven o'clock, so he (4) ________ (not cook) breakfast. My brother never (5) ________ (get) up early!

mark_scheme: Answer: doesn't cook / does not cook

u1.explanation: (1) and (2) happen 'right now', so they use am/is + -ing (sitting doubles the t). (3)–(5) are habits on weekdays, so they use the simple present: goes, doesn't cook, gets.

u1.stem:

Today is different. It is Saturday, and Leo is not at school. Right now, he is sitting in the living room. He is helping his grandfather to fix an old radio.

What is Leo doing right now?
options: He is taking the school bus.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Look at those dark clouds! It ________ rain.
u2.explanation: We can see the clouds, so we know it is coming: is going to + base verb.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

"I'm thirsty." "I ________ get you a glass of water."
u2.explanation: This is an offer decided right now, so we use will: I will (I'll) get you a glass of water.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

We ________ visit our cousins in Macau next weekend. We bought the ferry tickets yesterday.
u2.explanation: It is a plan made before (they bought tickets), so we use going to. 'We' goes with are: are going to.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

I think the test ________ easy tomorrow.
u2.explanation: 'I think' + a guess about the future → will + base verb: will be.

u2.stem:
Fill in the blank with the negative form of 'be going to'.

She ________ join the dance club this year. She is too busy.

mark_scheme: isn't going to / is not going to

u2.explanation: Negative of going to: is not (isn't) going to + base verb.

u2.stem:
Make a question for the word(s) in [square brackets].

They are going to have a party [next Friday].

mark_scheme: When are they going to have a party? (accept 'When are they going to have the party?')

u2.explanation: We ask about time with 'When'. Move 'are' before 'they': When are they going to have a party?

u2.stem:
Read the email and fill in the blanks with 'will' or the correct form of 'be going to'.

Hi Sam,
Next Saturday, my family (1) ________ (visit) the Science Museum. We planned it last week. My sister (2) ________ (bring) her camera. I think it (3) ________ (be) very interesting. Can you come too? I (4) ________ (ask) my mum to buy a ticket for you!
Luke
u2.explanation: (1) and (2) are plans made before, so we use going to. (3) is a guess with 'I think' → will be. (4) is an offer decided now → will ask.

u3.explanation: We compare it with all the mountains in Hong Kong, so we use the superlative: the highest.

u3.explanation: 'Interesting' is a long adjective, so we use more + adjective + than.

Choose the best answer.

My handwriting is bad, but my brother's handwriting is ________ (bad).
u3.explanation: 'Bad' is irregular: bad → worse → the worst.

Peter is 140 cm tall. Paul is 140 cm tall too.

mark_scheme: Peter is as tall as Paul. (accept 'Paul is as tall as Peter.')

u3.explanation: When two things are the same, we use as + adjective + as: Peter is as tall as Paul.

u3.stem:
Look at the information and fill in the blanks with the correct form of the given adjectives.

u4.stem:

u4.explanation: Apples can be counted, so we use 'How many'.

u4.stem:
Choose the best answer.

There isn't ________ milk in the fridge.
u4.explanation: In negative sentences we use 'any'. Milk is uncountable, so 'many' and 'a few' are wrong.

u4.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Please add ________ sugar to my tea. Not too much!
u4.explanation: Sugar is uncountable, and we want a small amount, so we use 'a little'.

u4.stem:
Choose the best answer.

There are ________ people on the bus. I can't find a seat!
u4.explanation: People can be counted, and there are more than we want: too many.

u4.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Ann made ________ mistakes than Joe in the test.
u4.explanation: Mistakes can be counted, so we use 'fewer'. 'Less' is for uncountable nouns like water or time.

u4.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the noun in brackets.

There are three ________ (box) on the table.
u4.explanation: Nouns ending in x add -es: box → boxes.

u4.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the noun in brackets.

The dentist checked all my ________ (tooth).

Words: any, a few, a little, much, many

Ben: How (1) ________ eggs do we need?
Dad: Only three. And we need (2) ________ oil for the pan.
Ben: How (3) ________ rice should I cook?
Dad: Two bowls. Do we have (4) ________ onions?
Ben: No, but we have (5) ________ carrots.

u7.stem:

u8.stem:
Read the text from 'An interview with the school caretaker'.

Our class newspaper team interviewed Mr Lau, the school caretaker.
Reporter: When did you start working at our school, Mr Lau?
Mr Lau: Twelve years ago.
Reporter: What time do you start work every day?
Mr Lau: I start at half past six. I open the gates and turn on the lights.
Reporter: What is the hardest part of your job?
Mr Lau: Fixing things on rainy days. Sometimes water comes into the hall.
Reporter: Which part of the school do you like best?

What is the hardest part of Mr Lau's job?
u8.explanation: Mr Lau says: 'Fixing things on rainy days.'

u9.stem:
Read the text from 'The Mid-Autumn Lantern Walk'.

The Mid-Autumn Festival is one of the most important festivals in Hong Kong. It falls on the fifteenth day of the eighth month of the lunar calendar, when the moon is at its brightest and roundest. Families get together, eat mooncakes and fruit such as pomelos, and go outside to admire the moon.

This year, Chloe's school held a lantern walk in the park near the school. The students made their own lanterns in their Art lessons. Chloe made a rabbit lantern from paper and bamboo sticks. It took her three lessons to finish it, and she was very proud of it.

On the evening of the walk, more than two hundred students and parents came. They walked slowly along the path by the lake, holding their glowing lanterns. Some of the lanterns were shaped like stars, fish and even rockets. Chloe walked with her grandmother, who told her the story of Chang'e, the lady who flew to the moon.

Suddenly, a strong wind blew, and the candle inside Chloe's lantern went out. Chloe felt disappointed. Then her grandmother took a small torch out of her bag and put it inside the lantern. "Now your rabbit can shine all night," she said with a smile. Chloe hugged her grandmother. It was her favourite Mid-Autumn Festival ever.

What is the passage mostly about?
options: Chloe's lantern walk at the Mid-Autumn Festival
a strong wind in the park
u9.explanation: Most of the passage tells about Chloe's school lantern walk at Mid-Autumn. The other answers are only small parts.

Read the text from 'The Mid-Autumn Lantern Walk'.

The Mid-Autumn Festival is one of the most important festivals in Hong Kong. It falls on the fifteenth day of the eighth month of the lunar calendar, when the moon is at its brightest and roundest. Families get together, eat mooncakes and fruit such as pomelos, and go outside to admire the moon.

This year, Chloe's school held a lantern walk in the park near the school. The students made their own lanterns in their Art lessons. Chloe made a rabbit lantern from paper and bamboo sticks. It took her three lessons to finish it, and she was very proud of it.

On the evening of the walk, more than two hundred students and parents came. They walked slowly along the path by the lake, holding their glowing lanterns. Some of the lanterns were shaped like stars, fish and even rockets. Chloe walked with her grandmother, who told her the story of Chang'e, the lady who flew to the moon.

Suddenly, a strong wind blew, and the candle inside Chloe's lantern went out. Chloe felt disappointed. Then her grandmother took a small torch out of her bag and put it inside the lantern. "Now your rabbit can shine all night," she said with a smile. Chloe hugged her grandmother. It was her favourite Mid-Autumn Festival ever.

What happened FIRST?
options: Chloe made her lantern in Art lessons.
Grandma put a torch in the lantern.
u9.explanation: The order is: Chloe made the lantern → the walk → the candle went out → Grandma put in a torch → Chloe hugged her.
